name: pokec
title: Pokec: who is influential, and where
description: Pokec social network: each row is a directed friendship from the first user to the second.

evidence.directed: 54.2% of rows are reciprocated: partial reciprocity is the signature of a directed graph; description says directed

steps.question: Who are the 10 most influential users?
steps.say: A first question. The plan, the reading of the file (directed, 30.6 million friendships) and the measure chosen for "influential" are on screen before the answer is trusted.

turn.question: Who are the 10 most influential users?

interpretation.measure: pagerank (influence = being linked to by other well-connected users, following friendship direction)

variants: in-degree (number of users who list this user as a friend)

steps.note: Influence on a directed friendship graph: PageRank weights each incoming link by the importance of the linking user, so it captures influence better than raw follower counts.
The 10 highest PageRank users.
Variant: in-degree, the number of incoming friendship links per user.
The 10 users with the most incoming links.

plan.rationale: The question says 'influential' without defining it, so PageRank on the directed graph is used because it accounts for who links to a user, not only how many. In-degree is computed as a simple alternative so the user can see whether the choice changes the ranking.

findings.detail: overlap@k=0.90; measures agree on the leaders

turn.explanation: The 10 most influential users, ranked by PageRank (damping 0.85) on the full directed graph of 1,632,803 nodes, are 5935, 5867, 1891, 6228, 8413, 57918, 27509, 1830, 25994 and 59973, led by node 5935 at 0.000383. Influence here means being linked to by other well-connected users, following edge direction, and the analysis used unweighted edges over all nodes rather than only the largest component. The PageRank scores sum to 1.000000, and no approximation was applied. Simple in-degree gives a similar list with 90% overlap at k=10 and the same leaders (5935, 5867, 1891, 6228). The main difference is that in-degree includes node 86306 (1,413 incoming links) where PageRank includes 27509, so the choice of measure changes the tail of the top 10 slightly.

references.the 20 most influential users: the top 20 by pagerank from turn 3

steps.note: Influence measure from turns 1 and 3, computed on the current whole graph.
The 20 most influential users.
Directed subgraph among the 20 users: only friendships between them.
Drop direction: two users are friends if linked in either direction. Input for the clique search.

plan.rationale: Pagerank top 20 gives the users; induced subgraph and undirected_graph prepare the 20-node friendship graph ignoring direction; the maximum clique search is then done by a short Python function because the catalogue has no clique operator.

patch.what: Take the top 20 most influential users (pagerank, as in turn 3) and find the largest mutually linked group among them, ignoring friendship direction.

plan.unsupported: The catalogue has no maximum-clique operator. Restricting to the top-20 pagerank users and ignoring direction (undirected_graph) gives the induced subgraph, but none of the listed operators (k_core, max_core, core_number, triangle_count, local_clustering, pairwise_distances) returns the largest set of mutually linked nodes or its members.
plan.code_task: Find the maximum clique of the undirected simple graph 'sub' (a clique is a set of nodes in which every two nodes are linked by an edge; direction is already dropped, so use adjacency regardless of edge direction). Return the clique size as the value and the sorted list of member node ids as the witness. If several maximum cliques have the same size, return the one whose sorted list of ids is lexicographically smallest when compared as integers; if the graph has no edges, return size 1 and the single smallest node id.
